svg.title: Figure 1b: recirculating Hankel coefficients and forward–adjoint pump switching
svg.desc: Functional architecture view of the simplified Hankel cell in Figure 1a. A recirculating fiber loop stores W(t) as time-multiplexed coefficient-comb pulses; t denotes time within the coefficient frame, and minus/plus superscripts denote old/updated state. Pulse silhouettes are schematic envelopes, not waveguide geometry or scalar representations of the complex coefficients. A weak directional read tap supplies copies of old W to one input of a true two-input, two-output Mach–Zehnder switch. Fixed M supplies the other input. The bar routing sends W to DFG pump 1 and M to DFG pump 2; the cross routing exchanges these assignments. The switch is outside the circulating-memory path. Persistent coefficients remain entirely outside the black box. After the weak read tap they traverse an external loop amplitude/phase trim, enter the upper input of a coherent injection coupler, and leave its selected upper output through external loop gain and fiber storage. The lower coupler input receives the cell’s weight increment Delta W, produced by its cross-SFG, coefficient filter and write amplitude/phase control. The other output is terminated. The selected output is a calibrated field sum, not an intrinsically lossless adder: loop trim/gain and the write scaling compensate coupler transfer factors, phases and passive losses in the effective update W_plus = W_minus + Delta W. Delta W labels the algorithmic increment with the optical interface calibration understood. With write enable off, no increment is injected and physical loss compensation preserves the state ideally. The loop has no old-weight injection input to the arithmetic cell; only a tapped pump copy enters it via the 2x2 switch. Logical retention is applied once per state update and is not implemented by unconditional decay on every lap. The black box retains the Figure 1a saved-forward-input port for the cross-SFG writer. Forward u=x and adjoint u=e use the same pair of DFGs, with separate sequential visits and no pipelining between heads. Old-state read copies must be held/replayed and aligned for both passes before writeback, including path delay to the second DFG. These holding/alignment elements and exact controller timing are abstracted by the note, not physically specified in this base panel. The write-enable line represents scheduling rather than a separate optical path. Full-comb pump-band switch response, coherent route phases, read-tap attenuation, loop loss/noise and gain remain design requirements. The diagram makes no numeric latency, switching-speed, loop-length or efficiency claim. Source sketch preserved; DejaVu Sans text and all artwork remain editable native SVG. Figure 1a waveguide colors and widths are preserved. Transparent background, no embedded raster images.
